results.snippet:
# I replaced my Twitter and Instagram accounts with RSSHub
```
https://rsshub.app/instagram/user/username   
(I also did youtube channels because why not)   
https://rsshub.app/youtube/user/username   
https://rsshub.app/youtube/channel/channel-id```    
*this site works with many other services, just check the docs for anything you might be interested in*

To preface, the only reason I use Instagram or Twitter is to follow the internet personalities I'm interested in. I had no reason to post anything, I was there for the updates. Though as a result of having an account for just updates, my twitter had hundreds of inferred interests of mine and I had to deactivate ~300 advertisers manually. Instagram, being owned by Facebook, is definitely doing the same thing except with 100% less end user control. If I'm not  even really taking part, then why do I have to consent to all this garbage???     
I'm making this in case anyone else has been looking for a solution to a similar problem.

A few days ago I found the RSSHub Docs and was a bit suprised to see something new claiming to work with Instagram and Twitter. Then it actually *did* work. I added all the accounts I actually cared about to a text file, then used some replace magic to add the preceding links to make them feeds.

I imported all the resulting links into [Flym](https://f-droid.org/app/net.frju.flym), and grouped them according to 'creed'. Now these updates I wanted from different places and different accounts all appear, organized in a single app. 

And the best part: I don't even need an account with these companies anymore. I don't need to consent to anything just to see that my dude said he's gonna stream soon or whatever.

TLDR: Visit the first link below, export your subscriptions, find an RSS reader that you like, and group your feeds.

[RSSHub Website/Documentation](https://docs.rsshub.app/en#twitter)   
[RSSHub Repo](https://github.com/DIYgod/RSSHub)    
*Disclaimers: The creator speaks and makes commits in Chinese.   
The Twitter RSS doesn't currenty support seeing replies or whats being retweeted, but it probably could with the right minds working on it*

I am in no way affiliated with RSSHub, nor its creators/supporters.
